key_insight: EpNet predicts complete crystal band structures directly from atomic coordinates using a learned empirical pseudopotential spanning 63 elements across the s, p and d blocks.
engineering_relevance: Fast band-structure and band-gap predictions could accelerate electronic-materials screening at about 1% of DFT computational cost.
method: Use an equivariant neural network to construct a Hamiltonian from local potentials and nonlocal projectors.
Train solely on band energies rather than DFT-derived Hamiltonian labels.
Predict band structures without costly DFT self-consistent iterations.
evidence_signal: On 600,000 structures from an independent database, the abstract reports overall band-gap errors less than half those of existing models.
watch_item: The abstract leaves median band-energy and band-gap errors as unresolved placeholders, limiting assessment of absolute accuracy on unseen chemical systems.
paper_title: Learning Electronic Band Structures Across the s, p, d Blocks with an Empirical Pseudopotential Network
